unit_name: Army Group G (Heeresgruppe G; Armeegruppe G until late 1944)
current_activity: Blaskowitz at Army Group G headquarters, Gérardmer, orders the XLVII Panzer Corps to Mirecourt-Neufchâteau
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 4 p. 192: "Blaskowitz, at his headquarters in Gerardmer, west of Colmar"; "On 4 September he finally reached Luettwitz by phone". Event definition: the headquarters at Gérardmer in the first week of September; 4 September is the day of the telephone call in the same sentence, so the place is documented for that day by implication only. Location: Gérardmer, Vosges, with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the day is that of the call, the place is stated in the text around it. Location support: CMH names the town. Commander: Generaloberst Johannes Blaskowitz.

unit_name: Army Group G (Heeresgruppe G; Armeegruppe G until late 1944)
location_qualifier: headquarters of 4 September; not documented for 8 September
current_activity: OB West places the First Army under Army Group G on 8 September
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 4 p. 193: "OB WEST replied on 8 September by transferring General Knobelsdorff's First Army from Army Group B to Army Group G"; Schramm p. 370, entry of 8 September: "Die 1. Armee, die der Armeegruppe G unterstellt wurde". Event definition: the day the First Army passes to Army Group G; the army group was still called Armeegruppe G (renamed Heeresgruppe G in force 11 September, next row). Event support: two families (CMH and the OKW war diary) give the same day. Location: Gérardmer, the headquarters CMH names on 4 September, with a precision of 25 km; no source read places the headquarters on 8 September. Location support fallback: fallback to the nearest dated headquarters (4 September). Commander: Generaloberst Johannes Blaskowitz.

unit_name: Army Group G (Heeresgruppe G; Armeegruppe G until late 1944)

current_activity: Armeegruppe G becomes Heeresgruppe G; the order of 9 September takes effect on 11 September
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary, p. 370, footnote: "Am 9. 9. wurde die Umwandlung der Armeegr. G. in die Heeresgr. G befohlen (in Kraft getreten am 11. 9.)". Event definition: the day the redesignation takes effect, 11 September; the order itself is dated 9 September in the same footnote. Event support: the footnote gives both days; no other source read gives the effective day. Location: Gérardmer, the headquarters CMH names on 4 September, with a precision of 25 km. Location support fallback: fallback to the nearest dated headquarters (4 September). Commander: Generaloberst Johannes Blaskowitz.

unit_name: Army Group G (Heeresgruppe G; Armeegruppe G until late 1944)
location_qualifier: headquarters of 4 September; not documented for 18 September
current_activity: Hitler replaces Blaskowitz with General Balck and orders the western Vosges position held
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary, p. 393, entry of 18 September: "ersetzte er den OB, Gen.-Oberst Blaskowitz, durch den Gen. d. Pz.-Tr. Balck". Event definition: the decision to replace Blaskowitz (18 September); Balck takes over command on 21 September in the next row (CMH and Lexikon), so the two rows are different events and not alternatives. Event support: the war diary dates the decision; no other source read gives it. Location: Gérardmer, the headquarters CMH names on 4 September, with a precision of 25 km. Location support fallback: fallback to the nearest dated headquarters (4 September). Commander: Generaloberst Johannes Blaskowitz.

unit_name: Army Group G (Heeresgruppe G; Armeegruppe G until late 1944)
location_qualifier: headquarters of 4 September; not documented for 21 September
current_activity: Balck takes over Army Group G from Blaskowitz; Mellenthin becomes chief of staff
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 5 p. 229-230: "On 21 September Hitler relieved General Blaskowitz and gave the command of Army Group G to General der Panzertruppen Hermann Balck"; "When Balck took over his new command on 21 September"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, Heeresgruppe G: Blaskowitz "8. Mai 1944 - 21. September 1944", Balck "21. September 1944 - 23. Dezember 1944". Event definition: the takeover of command on 21 September; Schramm's 18 September row is the decision. For the chief of staff the Lexikon gives Gyldenfeldt to 19 September and Mellenthin from 20 September, CMH has Mellenthin replacing Gyldenfeldt with Balck on 21 September; the difference is not a conflict about this row. Event support: CMH and the Lexikon (two families) agree on the day. Location: Gérardmer, the headquarters CMH names on 4 September, with a precision of 25 km. Location support fallback: fallback to the nearest dated headquarters (4 September). Commander: General der Panzertruppen Hermann Balck.
